newsitem.title: INDIA: ONGC asks Indian govmt to postpone divestment plan.
newsitem.headline: ONGC asks Indian govmt to postpone divestment plan.

text.p: India's state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC) has suggested to the government that it postpone the company's divestment plans in 1996/97 (April/March), its chairman said on Wednesday.
"We suggested it for two reasons. We don't need to raise funds this year for our exploration activity. If at all we will need it only next year," Bikash Bora told Reuters in an interview.
Bora said ONGC also wanted the divestment to be made in one chunk.
ONGC ranks 13th among non-U.S. oil companies with a reserve base of over 5,350 million tonnes of oil equivalent. The government holds 96 percent of the company's shares.
Bora said it had been telling the government that any divestment should be of a large portion of the firm, at least ten percent.
"Otherwise financial institutions will rather wait for next year if there is a large divestment going," he said.
Bora said ONGC last month appointed consultants McKinsey and Company to work out a restructuring and reorganisation of the company's operations.
"We will have a better story to tell next year," he said.
Bora said a decline in ONGC's crude production this year and poor share prices at the Bombay Stock Exchange were also reasons why the company had sought postponement of the divestment plans.

He said ONGC's crude oil output in 1996/97 was expected to fall to 29 million tonnes compared to last year's 31 million tonnes due to recovery problems in the western offshore fields. ONGC produces almost all of India's oil.
Bora said the Bombay High Basin in 1996/97 was expected to produce about 18.5 to 19 million tonnes compared to 21 million last year.
He also said ONGC was exploring a technology transfer agreement with some international oil companies to increase the recovery rate from the Bombay High and Neelam oil fields.
"Hopefully we should ask for some tenders in the format which will be acceptable to some of the oil companies," Bora said.
He said potentially there could be a tie up with some companies in the next six months.
Bora said ONGC was not planning to set any production targets for an enhanced oil recovery plan but was looking for a recovery rate of more than 40 percent of from the present 15 percent.
Referring to ONGC's overseas operations, Bora said the company had made offers to explore some blocks in Kazakhstan. If successful, agreements would be signed in three to four months.
He said the company was also working in Tunisia and Vietnam and looking at exploration possibilities in Nigeria, Sudan and Iraq, when a U.N. embargo against it is lifted.
